title: The Lantern of Willowbrook
premise: The lantern for tonight's autumn fair has gone dim. We are finding three little light charms to make it shine again.

chapters.title: Welcome to Willowbrook
chapters.goal: Learn how to play with Marmalade the cat.
chapters.recap: You were at home with Marmalade, getting ready for the day.

steps.text: Welcome to Willowbrook, a quiet village of gardens and friendly neighbours. You are the village detective, and everyone knows you are good at finding things.

steps.speaker: Dr. Rubinny
steps.text: Good morning, detective. I am Dr. Rubinny, and I will be your guide on this case. There is no hurry, and you can ask for help at any time.

steps.speaker: Marmalade
steps.text: Hello! I'm Marmalade. I will help you. Use the arrow buttons to move, and press OK to choose.

steps.goal: Let's practise. Can you find your reading glasses?
hints: Your reading glasses have two round lenses.

steps.speaker: Dr. Rubinny
steps.text: Well done! Now, some news. The lantern for tonight's autumn fair has gone dim. Three little light charms have rolled away around the village.
You are ready to begin. Let's visit the bakery first.

chat: What do you like to do on a quiet morning?
Have you ever had a cat or a dog? What was it like?

chapters.title: The Bakery
chapters.goal: Help Mrs. Bramble at the bakery and find the first light charm.
chapters.recap: You were at the bakery, helping Mrs. Bramble look for the first light charm.

steps.text: The bakery smells of warm bread. Mrs. Bramble is busy baking for the fair.

steps.speaker: Dr. Rubinny
steps.text: Our first stop is the bakery. Look carefully and take your time. Marmalade will help if you need it.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Bramble
steps.text: Good morning, detective! I was baking a pear tart for the fair when a little light charm rolled off my table. Could you help me tidy up first?

steps.goal: Find the honey pot, the loaf of bread and the strawberries.
hints: The honey pot is golden and round.
The loaf of bread is brown and crusty.
The strawberries are small and red.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Bramble
steps.text: Thank you, that's much tidier! My recipe cards are all mixed up. Each card has a twin. Could you put the pairs together?

steps.goal: Find two cards that are the same.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Bramble
steps.text: Lovely, all in pairs again! Now, a little question before we look for the charm.

steps.question: What fruit was Mrs. Bramble using in her tart?
steps.hint: She told you when you arrived. It is a sweet green fruit.

steps.speaker: Marmalade
steps.text: Look! Something is twinkling under the last recipe card. It's the first light charm!
You found the first light charm! Mrs. Bramble gives you a warm scone to say thank you. Two more charms to find.

chat: Did you ever bake bread or cakes? What did you like to make?
What was your favourite treat when you were young?
Which smells remind you of a warm kitchen?

chapters.title: The Garden
chapters.goal: Help Mr. Hollis in his garden and find the second light charm.
chapters.recap: You were in Mr. Hollis's garden, looking for the second light charm.

steps.text: Mr. Hollis's garden is bright with autumn colours. He is raking leaves into a tidy pile.

steps.speaker: Dr. Rubinny
steps.text: Here we are in the garden. Mr. Hollis would be glad of a sharp-eyed detective today.

steps.speaker: Mr. Hollis
steps.text: Hello, detective! I saw something sparkle near the flower beds, but my eyes aren't what they were. Shall we look together?

steps.goal: Find the ladybird, the mushroom and the chestnut.
hints: The ladybird is small and red with black spots.
The mushroom has a round cap and a little stalk.
The chestnut is shiny and brown.

steps.speaker: Mr. Hollis
steps.text: Thank you! Oh dear, my basket is all muddled. Some things belong in the garden, and some belong in the kitchen.

steps.goal: Put each thing where it belongs.

steps.speaker: Marmalade
steps.text: The sparkle is under the sleeping flowers. I know a kind spell to wake them for a moment. Watch, then do the same!

steps.goal: Watch the magic, then press the same symbols in the same order.

steps.speaker: Marmalade
steps.text: The flowers are opening! And look, there between the petals is the second light charm!

steps.speaker: Mr. Hollis
steps.text: Before you go, here is a riddle my grandmother used to tell me.

steps.question: I am tall and yellow, and I turn my face to the sun. What am I?
steps.hint: Think of a big, bright yellow flower.

steps.text: You found the second light charm! Mr. Hollis gives you a bunch of autumn flowers. Just one more charm to find.

chat: Did you ever have a garden? What did you like to grow?
Which season do you like best, and why?

chapters.title: The Library
chapters.goal: Help Miss Penrose at the library and find the third light charm.
chapters.recap: You were at the library, helping Miss Penrose look for the third light charm.

steps.text: The village library is quiet and warm. Tall shelves are full of books, and a clock ticks softly.

steps.speaker: Dr. Rubinny
steps.text: This is the library, our last stop before the fair. One more charm to find, and I know you can do it.

steps.speaker: Miss Penrose
steps.text: Welcome, detective! I was reading a lovely book about the sea when I heard a little tinkle. I think the last charm has rolled somewhere in here.

steps.goal: Find the magnifying glass, the candle and the key.
hints: The magnifying glass has a round glass and a handle.
The candle is tall, with a little flame on top.
The key is small and golden.

steps.speaker: Miss Penrose
steps.text: Thank you! People leave all sorts of things here. Books and papers go on the bookshelf, and hats and umbrellas go to the cloakroom.

steps.goal: Put each thing where it belongs.

steps.speaker: Marmalade
steps.text: Something glints behind the reading cards. Let's put the pairs together and look underneath!

steps.goal: Find two cards that are the same.

steps.speaker: Miss Penrose
steps.text: Lovely work! Before you look, a little question for a good detective.

steps.question: What was Miss Penrose's book about?
steps.hint: She told you when you arrived. Think of waves and boats.

steps.speaker: Marmalade
steps.text: Look under the last card! It's the third light charm, shining brightly!
You found the third light charm! Miss Penrose claps her hands. Now let's take all three charms to the village square.

chat: What kind of books or stories do you enjoy?
Did you have a favourite place to sit and read?
Is there a song or a poem you like?

chapters.title: The Lantern Lights Up
chapters.goal: Bring the three light charms to the lantern and light it for the fair.
chapters.recap: You were in the village square, getting ready to light the lantern.

steps.text: The village square is ready for the fair. There is bunting, a band, and a big lantern in the middle. Everyone has come to watch.

steps.speaker: Marmalade
steps.text: Here are the three light charms you found. Before we light the lantern, let's thank the friends who helped us.

steps.question: Who was baking a pear tart?
steps.hint: It was at the bakery, where the bread smelled so good.

steps.question: Who was raking leaves in the garden?
steps.hint: He looks after the flower beds.

steps.speaker: Marmalade
steps.text: Look, the lantern's light beads are all muddled on their string. Let's put three that match side by side, and they will glow!

steps.goal: Put three matching beads side by side, and they turn into light.

steps.speaker: Marmalade
steps.text: Now for the kindest spell of all. Watch the magic, then do the same, and the lantern will shine!

steps.goal: Watch the magic, then press the same symbols in the same order.

steps.text: The three charms glow, and the great lantern lights up with a warm golden light! Everyone cheers, and the band begins to play.

steps.speaker: Dr. Rubinny
steps.text: Wonderful work, detective. You found every charm, and Willowbrook is shining again. I am very proud of you.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Bramble
steps.text: Thank you, detective! The fair can begin. Willowbrook is lucky to have you.
You solved the mystery of the lantern! Enjoy the autumn fair, detective.

chat: Did you ever go to a fair or a street party? What was it like?
What music do you like to sing or dance to?
What makes a celebration special for you?
